- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or adjust downward by 3–7 points.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% of the deviation from forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5+ points lag), reduce forecast by 1–3% per day lag.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 1–2% to forecast to capture continuation.
